docs.title: Tessera
docs.text: The open-source data platform you run yourself. Connect and stream data, test and protect it, model it once, and give everyone dashboards, executive briefs and AI answers they can trust.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
docker run -d --name tessera -p 8710:8710 -v tessera-data:/data ghcr.io/vvipinthomas/tessera:latest

or with Python 3.11+:

bash pip install "https://github.com/vvipinthomas/tessera/releases/download/v1.7.4/tessera-1.7.4-py3-none-any.whl" tessera serve # http://127.0.0.1:8710 The console prints a one-time setup code; enter it in the browser and start in demo mode for a guided tour.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Tessera is one Python process that serves a web app and an API, runs background work (scheduler, pipeline workers, stream workers, alert and subscription delivery) and keeps all state in one folder.

                     ┌────────────────────────── Tessera process (FastAPI + uvicorn) ──────────────────────────┐
 browser (SPA) ─────▶│  auth: sessions, OIDC, API tokens, SCIM      security headers, CSP, rate limit, audit     │
 Power BI/Excel ────▶│  /odata   OData v4 feed (published data, masking + RLS)                                   │
 AI clients ────────▶│  /mcp     MCP server (governed tools, resources, prompts)                                 │
 webhooks/apps ─────▶│  /api/streams/{id}/events  HTTP push                                                      │
                     │                                                                                           │
                     │  connectors ──▶ ingest ──▶ raw ──transform──▶ curated ──quality──▶ PII scan ──publish──▶ serving
                     │  stream workers ──micro-batches──▶ raw                                     deliver ──▶ warehouses, lakes
                     │                                                                                           │
                     │  query guard (DuckDB parse tree) ─▶ RLS rewrite ─▶ result cache ─▶ DuckDB (no file/network access)
                     │  semantic models ─▶ insights, forecasts, executive brief ─▶ dashboards, reports, alerts, email
                     │  AI agents ─▶ tools (same guard, PII firewall, grounding check) ─▶ model providers              │
                     └──────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────┘
                                    ▼                                               ▼
                         tessera.db (SQLite, WAL)                        warehouse.duckdb
                         users, connections (secrets AES-GCM),           raw / curated / serving schemas
                         catalog, rules, pipelines, runs, models,
                         dashboards, streams, audit

docs.title: Security model
docs.text:
• Three zones. Data enters raw only through connectors and streams. Engineers transform it into curated. Publishing writes a masked copy into serving. Viewers, analysts, dashboards for them, OData, share links and AI agents acting for them can only read serving.
  • Query guard. Every interactive statement is parsed by DuckDB (json_serialize_sql). Only a single SELECT or EXPLAIN runs. Table references come from the parse tree, including CTEs and subqueries. DuckDB runs with enable_external_access=false, so SQL cannot read files, attach databases, install extensions or reach the network.
  • Row-level security. Policies map a published table's column to a user attribute. Before a restricted user's query runs, each reference to a protected table is rewritten to a per-query filtered view. This holds for SQL, Explore, dashboards, exports, subscriptions, alerts, forecasts, OData and AI tools.
  • Secrets. Connection passwords, tokens and model keys are encrypted with AES-256-GCM using master.key and are never returned by the API. API tokens, share tokens and stream tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes.
  • AI. Agents and MCP clients act with the caller's role. Tool results pass a PII firewall before reaching a model provider. Numbers in answers are checked against tool output, and repeated identical tool calls are refused.
  • Web. Content Security Policy script-src 'self', frame-ancestors 'none' (except allow-listed embeds), SameSite cookies plus a CSRF header, scrypt password hashing and lockout.

docs.title: Design decisions
docs.text: Decision Why Trade-off DuckDB + SQLite in one process Fast analytics on one machine, nothing else to install, simple backups One node; no horizontal scale-out Micro-batch streaming with positions saved after the write At-least-once delivery without a distributed log or checkpoint store Seconds of latency; not a stream processor Arrow everywhere between connectors and the warehouse Zero-copy loads and automatic schema evolution Very wide nested JSON is flattened No front-end framework Small, auditable, strict CSP, no build step More hand-written DOM code Statistical forecasting chosen by holdout accuracy Explainable, cheap, honest about error No external drivers (promotions, prices) SQL and Markdown notebooks only Running user code would bypass permissions No Python in notebooks OData rather than a Postgres wire endpoint Native connectors in Power BI, Excel and Tableau, stateless, easy to secure Read-only; no DirectQuery

docs.title: Tessera on Cloudflare
docs.text:
Run the complete Tessera, with all 25 connectors, streams, pipelines, dashboards and AI, on Cloudflare. Nothing is cut down: Cloudflare runs the same container image you would run anywhere else, and Cloudflare R2 keeps its data.

 people, Power BI, AI clients ──HTTPS──▶  Worker  ──────────▶  Tessera container  ──backups──▶  R2 bucket
                                      (front door,          (Python, DuckDB, every        (latest state,
                                       Access, cron)         connector and stream)         restored on start)
Piece Cloudflare product Job Front door Workers TLS, your domain, optional Cloudflare Access sign-in, wakes and keeps Tessera running, shows a "starting" page Tessera Containers The full application, built from this repository's Dockerfile Durable storage R2 Consistent backups every few minutes, after every pipeline run and on every shutdown; restored automatically Your lakehouse (optional) R2, R2 Data Catalog Delta and Iceberg tables Tessera reads and writes AI (optional) Workers AI, AI Gateway Models for Tessera's agents, or a gateway in front of Anthropic and OpenAI

docs.title: Why it works this way
docs.text:
Cloudflare Containers give each container a fresh disk whenever it sleeps, restarts or is replaced by a deploy. Tessera keeps its data on disk (SQLite and DuckDB), so on Cloudflare it runs in cloud mode (tessera cloud-run):

  • On start, a container with an empty disk restores the newest backup from R2.
  • While running, Tessera writes a consistent backup to R2 every 5 minutes when anything changed, and straight after every pipeline run.
  • On shutdown (sleep, deploy, platform maintenance), Cloudflare sends SIGTERM; Tessera stops pipelines and streams, writes a final backup, then exits.

A planned stop loses nothing. An unplanned crash loses at most the changes since the last backup (5 minutes by default, configurable). The encryption key is not stored in R2: it lives in Workers secrets and is handed to the container at start.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• A Cloudflare account on the Workers Paid plan (Containers require it).
  • Docker running on the machine you deploy from: Wrangler builds the image locally and pushes it to Cloudflare.
  • Node.js 20 or newer.
  • About 20 minutes.

docs.title: Deploy
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/vvipinthomas/tessera.git
cd tessera/cloudflare
npm ci
npx wrangler login

1. Create the bucket for Tessera's data

npx wrangler r2 bucket create tessera-data

2. Create an R2 API token so the container can write backups. In the Cloudflare dashboard: R2 → Manage API tokens → Create API token, permission Object Read & Write, limited to the tessera-data bucket. Copy the Access Key ID, the Secret Access Key and your Account ID (shown on the R2 overview page).

3. Store the secrets

# The key that encrypts saved connection passwords. Keep a copy in your password manager:
# without it, a restored Tessera cannot read the passwords it saved.
python3 -c "import os,base64;print(base64.b64encode(os.urandom(32)).decode())"
npx wrangler secret put TESSERA_MASTER_KEY

npx wrangler secret put TESSERA_SETUP_CODE                 # any phrase of 8+ characters, used once to create the admin
npx wrangler secret put R2_ACCOUNT_ID
npx wrangler secret put TESSERA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_ID
npx wrangler secret put TESSERA_CLOUD_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY

4. Deploy

npx wrangler deploy

Wrangler builds the image, uploads it and prints the address, for example https://tessera.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev. The first deploy can take several minutes while Cloudflare provisions the container.

5. Open it. You will see Tessera is starting for up to a minute, then the setup screen. Enter your setup code, create the admin account, and leave Start in demo mode ticked if you want the guided tour.

Deploying from GitHub instead (no computer needed). Add CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID and the four TESSERA_* secrets from step 3 as repository secrets, then run Actions → Deploy to Cloudflare. The workflow creates the bucket, deploys and sets the Worker's secrets. Step by step, from a phone: CLOUDFLARE_MOBILE.md.

docs.title: Your own domain
docs.text:
Dashboard: Workers & Pages → tessera → Settings → Domains & Routes → Add → Custom domain, for example data.example.com. Then tell Tessera its public address (used in emails, share links, SSO and the OData feed):

// cloudflare/wrangler.jsonc → "vars"
"TESSERA_BASE_URL": "https://data.example.com"

and run npx wrangler deploy again.

docs.title: Sign-in with Cloudflare Access (optional)
docs.text: Zero Trust → Access → Applications → Add an application → Self-hosted for your Tessera domain, with a policy such as "emails ending in @example.com". Add Bypass policies for the paths machines call with their own tokens: /odata/*, /mcp, /api/streams/*/events, /scim/v2/* and /api/auth/oidc/callback. Tessera's own roles, workspaces and row-level security still apply after Access lets someone in.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Put plain settings in "vars" in wrangler.jsonc; put anything sensitive in a secret (npx wrangler secret put). Every variable whose name starts with TESSERA_ is passed to the container, so everything in CONFIGURATION.md works here too.

Setting Default What it does TESSERA_CLOUD_BACKUP_MINUTES 5 How often to back up when something changed. Lower means less to lose in a crash TESSERA_CLOUD_KEEP 48 Backups to keep in R2 (older ones are deleted) TESSERA_CLOUD_BUCKET tessera-data The bucket for backups TESSERA_CLOUD_PREFIX tessera/ Folder inside the bucket, so one bucket can hold several Tesseras KEEP_WARM true A cron pings Tessera every 5 minutes so it never sleeps and schedules, alerts and streams run on time. Set false to let it sleep when nobody uses it (cheaper; scheduled work then waits until the next visit) SLEEP_AFTER 30m How long without requests before an idle Tessera sleeps (only matters when KEEP_WARM is false) instance_type standard-3 2 vCPU, 8 GiB memory, 16 GB disk. Use standard-4 (4 vCPU, 12 GiB, 20 GB) for larger data

docs.title: Operating it
docs.text: Task How Is it running? https://<your tessera>/__tessera/status Logs npx wrangler tail, or Workers & Pages → tessera → Logs (container logs under Containers) Backup status, back up now Admin → Operations → Cloud backups in Tessera See the backups R2 → tessera-data → tessera/backups/ Upgrade git pull && npx wrangler deploy. The old container writes its final backup, the new one restores it. Visitors see the starting page for about a minute Go back to an earlier point Add "TESSERA_CLOUD_RESTORE_KEY": "backups/tessera-<time>.tar.gz" to vars and deploy. The new container restores that backup once and makes it the latest; remove the setting afterwards Move off Cloudflare Download the latest backup from R2 and tessera restore it on a server or AWS (see DEPLOY.md) with the same master key

docs.title: Your lakehouse on R2
docs.text:
Tessera reads and writes open table formats directly on R2, so your data stays in your account in formats Spark, Databricks, Snowflake, DuckDB and Trino can read too.

Iceberg with R2 Data Catalog. Turn on the catalog for a bucket (R2 → bucket → Settings → R2 Data Catalog), and create an API token with R2 and Data Catalog permissions. In Tessera: Connections → New → Apache Iceberg tables:

Field Value Catalog rest Catalog URI the Catalog URI shown on the bucket's settings page Warehouse the Warehouse name shown there Token the API token

Delta tables on R2. Connections → New → Delta Lake tables with folder s3://<bucket>/lake and storage options:

{"AWS_ENDPOINT_URL": "https://<account id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com", "AWS_REGION": "auto",
 "AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID": "<key id>", "AWS_S3_ALLOW_UNSAFE_RENAME": "true"}

and the secret key in the encrypted Storage secret field. Add a Deliver step to a pipeline to publish gold tables there. (AWS_S3_ALLOW_UNSAFE_RENAME is safe while Tessera is the only writer to those tables.)

Plain files. The S3 connector works with R2: bucket name, endpoint https://<account id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com, region auto, and the key pair.

docs.title: AI on Cloudflare
docs.text:
• Workers AI: Admin → AI providers → Cloudflare Workers AI. Base URL https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/<account id>/ai/v1, an API token with Workers AI permission, and a model that supports function calling (Tessera's agents call tools), for example a Llama 3.3 70B instruct model.
  • AI Gateway in front of Anthropic or OpenAI (caching, rate limits, logs): keep the provider type, and set its base URL to the gateway's, for example https://gateway.ai.cloudflare.com/v1/<account id>/<gateway>/anthropic.

docs.title: Limits to know
docs.text:
• One instance. Tessera is a single-server product, so max_instances is 1. Size it with instance_type.
  • Data size. The warehouse must fit the container disk (16 GB on standard-3, 20 GB on standard-4, with room for temporary files) and be backed up within the interval; a few gigabytes is comfortable. Larger data belongs in R2 as Delta or Iceberg tables, or in a warehouse Tessera reads from.
  • Crash window. An unplanned crash can lose up to TESSERA_CLOUD_BACKUP_MINUTES of changes. Pipelines can simply be re-run; HTTP push senders should retry on errors.
  • Uploads through the Worker are limited by your Cloudflare plan's request body size (100 MB on most plans). Load bigger files from R2 or S3 with a connector instead.
  • Inbound traffic is HTTP only. That covers the app, the API, OData, MCP and HTTP push. Streams read from Kafka, Event Hubs, Kinesis and MQTT, which works because containers can connect out.

docs.title: Running it without Containers
docs.text: If you prefer to run Tessera on your own server and only use Cloudflare in front of it (no inbound ports, Access, WAF), use a Cloudflare Tunnel instead: see DEPLOY.md → Cloudflare.

docs.title: Deploy Tessera to Cloudflare from your phone and test it on Android
docs.text:
You can do everything here in Chrome on an Android phone, without a computer. GitHub builds Tessera and deploys it to your Cloudflare account. You then open it on the phone like an app.

Time: about 30 minutes. Most of it is waiting for the first build. Cost: Cloudflare's Workers Paid plan ($5 a month, required for Containers), plus any container usage above what the plan includes. Check Cloudflare's Containers pricing; Lower the cost shows how to save.

Tip: Cloudflare's and GitHub's settings pages fit better in Chrome with ⋮ → Desktop site switched on.

docs.title: Part 1: Put the code on GitHub
docs.text:
1. In Chrome go to github.com/new, or open the GitHub app and tap + → Create repository.
  2. Name it tessera. Leave README, .gitignore and licence unticked so the repository is empty. Tap Create.
  3. Send Claude the message "done" and Claude pushes the code. If you are pushing it yourself, push the main branch with its tags.

docs.title: Part 2: Prepare Cloudflare
docs.text:
Sign in at dash.cloudflare.com.

# Do this Keep 1 Workers & Pages → Plans, then choose Workers Paid — 2 Workers & Pages → Overview: copy the Account ID shown on the right (on a phone, scroll down) Account ID 3 R2 Object Storage → Create bucket, name it tessera-data, then Create — 4 R2 → Manage API tokens → Create API token. Permission Object Read & Write, applied to the tessera-data bucket. Create, then copy both keys. The secret is shown only once R2 Access Key ID, R2 Secret Access Key 5 My Profile → API Tokens → Create Token → Edit Cloudflare Workers (Use template). Under Permissions, add Account · Workers R2 Storage · Edit and Account · Containers · Edit. Set Account Resources to your account. Continue → Create Token, then copy it Cloudflare API token

About step 5: Cloudflare's permission names change from time to time. If the deploy later fails with an Authentication error, edit the token and add any Containers or Cloudchamber permission the list offers.

docs.title: Two values you make yourself
docs.text:
• Master key. It encrypts saved connection passwords and must be exactly 32 random bytes in base64.
  • On Android, install Termux and run openssl rand -base64 32 (if openssl is missing, run pkg install openssl first).
  • Or ask Claude to generate one.
  • Save it in your password manager. If you lose it, a restored Tessera cannot read the passwords it saved.
  • Setup code. Any phrase of 8 or more characters. You type it once to create the admin account.

docs.title: Part 3: Give GitHub the secrets and deploy
docs.text:
1. In your tessera repository go to Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret.
  2. Add these six secrets. Names must match exactly:
Name Value CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN the Cloudflare API token from step 5 CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID the Account ID from step 2 TESSERA_MASTER_KEY your master key TESSERA_SETUP_CODE your setup code TESSERA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_ID the R2 Access Key ID from step 4 TESSERA_CLOUD_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY the R2 Secret Access Key from step 4
  1. Open the Actions tab. The first time, tap I understand my workflows, go ahead and enable them.
  2. Tap Deploy to Cloudflare → Run workflow → Run workflow (branch main).
  3. Wait for the green tick. The first run takes 10 to 15 minutes while it builds the container image.
  4. Open the run, then the Deploy step. Near the end it shows your address, for example https://tessera.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev. You can also find it at Cloudflare → Workers & Pages → tessera → Visit.

The workflow creates the bucket if it is missing, deploys, and copies the four TESSERA_* secrets into the Worker. Later runs only update the code.

docs.title: First start
docs.text:
1. Open the address in Chrome. You will see Tessera is starting for up to a minute, or a few minutes on the very first deploy while Cloudflare provisions the container. It refreshes by itself.
  2. To check on it, open https://<your address>/__tessera/status. When it shows "container": "healthy", Tessera is up.
  3. On the setup screen:
  4. Enter your setup code.
  5. Create the admin account (email, name, a strong password).
  6. Leave Start in demo mode ticked to get sample data, dashboards and pipelines.
  7. In Chrome tap ⋮ → Add to Home screen. Tessera then opens from its own icon.

docs.title: What to try
docs.text: Area Test You should see Layout Use it upright, then turn the phone sideways Pages fit the screen; the sections are an icon strip along the top that you can swipe Executive brief Open Brief Headline numbers, forecasts and plain-language notes Dashboards Open a demo dashboard and tap a chart Values on tap; tapping a bar filters the other charts Catalog Catalog → a serving dataset → Preview, Profile, Lineage Data, column statistics and the lineage graph Upload from the phone Catalog → Upload, pick a CSV from Downloads or Drive A new raw. table with its row count SQL SQL, run select * from serving.<a demo table> limit 20 Results in a scrollable table Pipelines Pipelines → a demo pipeline → Run Status changes to success, with the step log Quality and privacy Dataset → Quality → Run; Scan for personal data Rule results; personal-data columns flagged and masked Streams Streams (demo) Live events counting up Dark mode Switch Android to dark theme Tessera follows it Backups Admin → Operations → Cloud backups → Back up now Last backup updates. In Cloudflare, R2 → tessera-data → tessera/backups/ shows the file AI (optional) Admin → AI providers, add a key (Anthropic, OpenAI or Cloudflare Workers AI), then ask a question in Agents An answer with the SQL it ran

docs.title: Check that your data survives a restart
docs.text:
1. Make a change, for example upload a CSV.
  2. In GitHub run Deploy to Cloudflare again. This replaces the container.
  3. Wait for the starting page to clear, then sign in. Your upload is still there, restored from R2.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text: Symptom Fix Workflow fails at Deploy with Authentication error The API token is missing a permission. Add the Containers and R2 Storage edit permissions (Part 2, step 5) and run again Workflow says Containers are not available The account is not on Workers Paid yet Stuck on Tessera is starting for more than 10 minutes Cloudflare → Workers & Pages → tessera → Logs (container logs are under Containers). The usual cause is a missing or wrongly formatted TESSERA_MASTER_KEY: fix the GitHub secret and run the workflow again Setup code is rejected Check TESSERA_SETUP_CODE in GitHub, run the workflow again, then retry Back up now shows an error The R2 key pair is wrong or not allowed on tessera-data. Make a new R2 token, update the two TESSERA_CLOUD_* secrets, run the workflow Everything is slow after a quiet period The container was sleeping. Keep KEEP_WARM at true (the default)

docs.title: Lower the cost
docs.text: By default, a cron job wakes Tessera every 5 minutes, so schedules and streams run on time. That keeps the container running all day. To let it sleep when nobody uses it, set "KEEP_WARM": "false" in cloudflare/wrangler.jsonc. You can edit the file in GitHub's web editor (the pencil icon), commit, then run the workflow. With KEEP_WARM off, scheduled work waits until the next visit.

docs.title: Use your own domain (optional)
docs.text:
1. In Cloudflare, go to Workers & Pages → tessera → Settings → Domains & Routes → Add → Custom domain, for example data.example.com.
  2. In cloudflare/wrangler.jsonc, add "TESSERA_BASE_URL": "https://data.example.com" under vars.
  3. Commit, then run the workflow.

More detail, including Cloudflare Access sign-in and your lakehouse on R2, is in CLOUDFLARE.md.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Tessera reads its settings from environment variables at start-up. Everything else (users, SSO, email, AI providers, sharing, OpenLineage, retention) is set in the app under Admin and stored in the data folder.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Variable Default What it does TESSERA_DATA_DIR ./tessera-data The data folder: metadata database, DuckDB warehouse, uploads, exports, master.key TESSERA_HOST 127.0.0.1 Address to listen on. The container image uses 0.0.0.0 TESSERA_PORT 8710 Port to listen on TESSERA_BASE_URL – Public address, for example https://tessera.example.com. Used for SSO redirects, links in emails, the OData feed and share links TESSERA_SECURE_COOKIES false Set true whenever people reach Tessera over HTTPS. Adds Secure cookies and HSTS TESSERA_SESSION_HOURS 12 How long a sign-in lasts TESSERA_MASTER_KEY generated Base64 32-byte key that encrypts stored secrets. If unset, master.key is created in the data folder. Generate one with python -c "import os,base64;print(base64.b64encode(os.urandom(32)).decode())" TESSERA_IMPORT_DIRS – Extra server folders the Files, SQLite, Delta and Iceberg connectors may read, separated by : (; on Windows) TESSERA_MAX_UPLOAD_MB 512 Largest file accepted by the upload page TESSERA_TIMEZONE UTC Time zone for pipeline, alert and subscription schedules, for example America/Vancouver TESSERA_WORKERS 2 Pipeline runs that may execute at the same time TESSERA_SCHEDULER_INTERVAL 20 Seconds between scheduler checks TESSERA_RETRY_BASE_SECONDS 2 First retry delay for failing pipeline steps (doubles each attempt) TESSERA_QUERY_TIMEOUT 60 Seconds before an interactive query is cancelled TESSERA_MAX_RESULT_ROWS 10000 Row limit for interactive results (exports and OData page through larger results) TESSERA_BLOCK_PRIVATE_HTTP false Stop REST, Iceberg REST, OpenLineage, streaming and SFTP connections from reaching private network addresses. Cloud metadata and link-local addresses are always blocked TESSERA_RATE_LIMIT 1200 API requests per minute per caller (token, session or IP) TESSERA_METRICS_TOKEN – Bearer token that may read /metrics (otherwise an admin session is required) TESSERA_LOG_JSON false JSON log lines with request IDs, and an access log TESSERA_MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS – Extra browser origins allowed to call /mcp, comma-separated TESSERA_TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS false Use the first X-Forwarded-For address as the caller's address (sign-in lockout, rate limits, audit). Turn on only when Tessera is reachable solely through your proxy TESSERA_SETUP_CODE generated Set the one-time setup code yourself (8+ characters) instead of reading it from the console; useful on hosted platforms

docs.title: Cloud mode (tessera cloud-run)
docs.text:
For hosts whose disk does not survive a restart. See CLOUDFLARE.md.

Variable Default What it does TESSERA_CLOUD_BUCKET – S3-compatible bucket for backups (required) TESSERA_CLOUD_ENDPOINT AWS S3 Endpoint, for Cloudflare R2 https://<account id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com TESSERA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_ID / TESSERA_CLOUD_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY – Credentials (or the platform's own role on AWS) TESSERA_CLOUD_REGION auto Region (R2 uses auto) TESSERA_CLOUD_PREFIX tessera/ Folder inside the bucket TESSERA_CLOUD_BACKUP_MINUTES 5 Back up this often when anything changed (also after every pipeline run and on shutdown) TESSERA_CLOUD_KEEP 48 Backups to keep TESSERA_CLOUD_RESTORE_KEY – Restore this backup instead of the latest, once

Cloud mode requires TESSERA_MASTER_KEY, because backups deliberately leave the key out.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
tessera serve [--host 0.0.0.0] [--port 8710]          run the server
tessera create-user someone@example.com --role engineer
tessera reset-password someone@example.com            also unlocks the account
tessera backup --out backup.tar.gz [--include-key]    stop the server first, or use Admin → Operations
tessera restore backup.tar.gz [--force]
tessera mcp --url https://tessera.example.com         MCP stdio bridge for desktop AI clients (token in TESSERA_TOKEN)
tessera cloud-run [--port 8710]                       run with data kept in an S3/R2 bucket (cloud mode)
tessera version

Every command accepts --data-dir before the sub-command, for example tessera --data-dir /srv/tessera serve.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Role Can viewer Open dashboards, reports and published datasets; ask questions; read the catalog and glossary analyst Everything a viewer can, plus SQL on published data, Explore, building reports and dashboards, alerts, subscriptions, AI agents and watching streams engineer Everything an analyst can, plus connections, streams, pipelines, transforms, quality rules, raw and curated data, models admin Everything, plus users, SSO, SCIM, email, AI providers, row-level security, integrations, sharing, backups and the audit log

Workspaces add per-workspace roles (viewer, contributor, admin) on top; see ENTERPRISE.md.

docs.title: Health and monitoring endpoints
docs.text: Endpoint Use /api/health Liveness: the process answers /api/ready Readiness: metadata and warehouse are reachable (use for load balancers and container health checks) /metrics Prometheus metrics: requests, latency, pipeline runs, query cache /api/docs Interactive REST API reference

docs.title: Deploying Tessera
docs.text:
Tessera is a single Python process. It keeps all of its state in one data folder: tessera.db (SQLite metadata), warehouse.duckdb (the analytical store), imports/, exports/ and master.key. Three things matter wherever you run it:

  1. A persistent disk for the data folder. Anything that wipes the disk on restart, sleep or rescheduling loses data.
  2. HTTPS in front of it, with TESSERA_SECURE_COOKIES=true and TESSERA_BASE_URL set to the public address.
  3. Backups of the data folder, including master.key (without it, stored connection passwords cannot be decrypted).

Run exactly one Tessera process per data folder. It is not designed for several replicas sharing a disk.

Option Good for Effort Your computer Trying it, personal analysis 2 minutes Any server with Docker A team on a VM you already have 10 minutes AWS A managed, backed-up install from one template 15 minutes Cloudflare Containers Running all of Tessera on Cloudflare, with data kept in R2 and no server to manage 20 minutes Cloudflare from a phone The same, deployed through GitHub Actions without a computer 30 minutes Cloudflare Tunnel Publishing a Tessera that runs on your own server, without opening ports, behind single sign-on 20 minutes

Sizing: 2 vCPU and 8 GB RAM serve a team of dozens with tens of gigabytes. DuckDB uses memory first and spills to disk, so give the data volume room for about twice your largest table. On a 2-vCPU machine a mixed load ran at about 160 requests per second with p95 latency near 130 ms.

docs.title: Your computer
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/vvipinthomas/tessera.git && cd tessera
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[s3,kafka,mqtt,iceberg,sftp,delta,mongodb]"
tessera serve                       # http://127.0.0.1:8710

tessera serve listens on 127.0.0.1 only. To reach it from other machines on your network, use tessera serve --host 0.0.0.0 and put HTTPS in front before anyone signs in from elsewhere.

On Windows, use PowerShell and .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1. Everything else is the same.

docs.title: Any server with Docker
docs.text:
Works on any Linux VM (Ubuntu, Debian, Amazon Linux, RHEL), on-premises or in any cloud.

# 1. Install Docker Engine and the Compose plugin: https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/
git clone https://github.com/vvipinthomas/tessera.git && cd tessera

# 2a. HTTP on port 8710 (inside a private network only)
docker compose up -d --build

# 2b. HTTPS with an automatic Let's Encrypt certificate
#     First point a DNS A record at this server and open ports 80 and 443.
TESSERA_DOMAIN=tessera.example.com \
  docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f deploy/https/docker-compose.https.yml up -d --build

# 3. Read the one-time setup code and open the site
docker compose logs tessera | grep "Setup code"

The HTTPS file adds a Caddy container that obtains and renews the certificate, removes the direct port, and turns on secure cookies. Put TESSERA_DOMAIN=... in a .env file next to docker-compose.yml so later commands pick it up.

Where the data is. In the tessera-data Docker volume. To keep it in a folder you choose instead, add a docker-compose.override.yml:

services:
  tessera:
    volumes: !override
      - /srv/tessera/data:/data

and run sudo chown -R 10001:10001 /srv/tessera/data once (the container runs as user 10001, not root).

Upgrading. git pull && docker compose up -d --build. Database changes are applied automatically at start-up. Take a backup first.

docs.title: AWS
docs.text:
The template deploy/aws/tessera-ec2.yaml creates everything in one stack:

Resource Why EC2 instance (Amazon Linux 2023, Docker) Runs Tessera and, when you give a domain, Caddy for HTTPS Encrypted gp3 EBS data volume mounted at /srv/tessera Holds the data folder. Snapshotted, not deleted, if the stack is deleted Elastic IP A stable address for your DNS record Private, versioned, encrypted S3 bucket Nightly consistent backups, kept 35 days. Retained if the stack is deleted IAM role with Systems Manager Shell access through Session Manager, so no SSH port is open Security group 443 (and 80 for the certificate) from the range you choose

docs.title: Create the stack
docs.text:
Console: CloudFormation → Create stack → Upload a template file → deploy/aws/tessera-ec2.yaml.

Or with the AWS CLI:

aws cloudformation deploy \
  --stack-name tessera \
  --template-file deploy/aws/tessera-ec2.yaml \
  --capabilities CAPABILITY_IAM \
  --parameter-overrides DomainName=tessera.example.com AllowedCidr=203.0.113.0/24 InstanceType=m7i.large DataVolumeGiB=100

aws cloudformation describe-stacks --stack-name tessera --query "Stacks[0].Outputs"

Then:

  1. DNS. Create an A record for your domain pointing at the PublicIp output. Caddy gets the certificate on the first request after the record resolves (a minute or two). Without a domain, Tessera is at http://<PublicIp>:8710; use that only from a trusted network.
  2. Setup code. Connect with Session Manager (aws ssm start-session --target <instance-id>, or EC2 → Connect → Session Manager in the console) and run sudo cat /srv/tessera/data/setup-code.txt. Setup takes about five minutes after the stack completes; progress is in /var/log/tessera-setup.log.
  3. Open the URL, enter the code and create the admin.

docs.title: Backups and restore
docs.text:
A cron job runs /usr/local/bin/tessera-backup at the hour you chose. It stops Tessera for a few seconds, writes a checksummed archive with tessera backup --include-key, starts Tessera, and uploads the archive to s3://<BackupBucket>/backups/. The archive contains master.key, which is why the bucket blocks public access, requires TLS and is encrypted. Logs are in /var/log/tessera-backup.log.

To restore onto a new instance:

aws s3 cp s3://<BackupBucket>/backups/tessera-backup-<time>.tar.gz /tmp/
cd /opt/tessera && $(cat .compose-cmd) stop tessera
$(cat .compose-cmd) run --rm --no-deps -v /tmp:/restore tessera tessera restore /restore/tessera-backup-<time>.tar.gz --force
$(cat .compose-cmd) start tessera

docs.title: Upgrading on AWS
docs.text:
cd /opt/tessera && sudo git fetch --tags && sudo git checkout v1.5.1   # the new tag
sudo $(cat .compose-cmd) up -d --build

docs.title: Other AWS options
docs.text:
• Amazon ECS on EC2 works with the same container image if you pin the task to one instance and mount an EBS volume (or a host path) at /data. Run one task only.
  • AWS Fargate with EFS, App Runner, Lambda and Lightsail containers are not recommended. Fargate and App Runner disks are temporary; EFS is a network file system, which DuckDB and SQLite do not handle well for locking or speed; Lambda cannot keep a server running.
  • Load balancer instead of Caddy: put an Application Load Balancer with an ACM certificate in front of port 8710, set TESSERA_SECURE_COOKIES=true and TESSERA_BASE_URL, and set the target group health check to /api/ready.
  • Snapshots: you can add an Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager policy for daily EBS snapshots of the data volume as a second layer of protection.

docs.title: Cloudflare
docs.text:
There are two ways to use Cloudflare:

  • Run Tessera on Cloudflare with Containers, a Worker in front and data kept in R2. No server to manage. See CLOUDFLARE.md.
  • Publish a Tessera that runs on your own server through a Cloudflare Tunnel, described here. Use this when the data must stay on your hardware, or when the warehouse is too big for a container's disk.

The tunnel setup:

browser ──HTTPS──▶ Cloudflare edge (TLS, WAF, optional Access SSO) ──Tunnel──▶ cloudflared ──▶ Tessera on your server

Tessera runs on any machine you have (an office server, a home lab, a VM in any cloud). The machine needs no open inbound ports: cloudflared makes an outbound connection to Cloudflare.

docs.title: 1. Create the tunnel
docs.text:
1. In the Cloudflare dashboard, open Zero Trust → Networks → Tunnels → Create a tunnel, choose Cloudflared, name it tessera, and copy the token shown in the install command.
  2. Under Public hostnames, add tessera.example.com (a domain on your Cloudflare account) with service type HTTP and URL tessera:8710.

docs.title: 2. Start Tessera with the tunnel
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/vvipinthomas/tessera.git && cd tessera
cat > .env <<'EOF'
TUNNEL_TOKEN=<token from step 1>
TESSERA_DOMAIN=tessera.example.com
EOF
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f deploy/cloudflare/docker-compose.tunnel.yml up -d --build
docker compose logs tessera | grep "Setup code"

Open https://tessera.example.com. Tessera's port is not published on the host at all; only the tunnel can reach it.

docs.title: 3. Optional: Cloudflare Access in front
docs.text:
Access adds your identity provider's sign-in before anyone reaches Tessera's own sign-in page.

  1. Zero Trust → Access → Applications → Add an application → Self-hosted, domain tessera.example.com, with a policy such as "emails ending in @example.com".
  2. Machines also call Tessera, so add Bypass (or service-token) policies for these paths, which carry their own tokens:
  3. /odata/* (Power BI, Excel, Tableau)
  4. /mcp (AI clients)
  5. /api/streams/*/events (HTTP push streams)
  6. /scim/v2/* (user provisioning from Entra ID or Okta)
  7. /api/auth/oidc/callback if you also use Tessera's own SSO
  8. If you use Tessera's built-in OpenID Connect SSO as well, people sign in twice. Many teams use Access for the network boundary and Tessera SSO for roles; both work.

docs.title: 4. Optional: the landing page on Cloudflare Pages
docs.text:
The marketing page can be built as one static file and hosted for free:

python scripts/build_artifact.py site/index.html
npx wrangler pages deploy site --project-name tessera-site

docs.title: Backups with Cloudflare
docs.text: Cloudflare does not hold any Tessera data. Back up the server's data folder as in Backups, for example to Cloudflare R2 with any S3 tool: aws s3 cp backup.tar.gz s3://bucket/ --endpoint-url https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com.

docs.title: Backups
docs.text:
Method Downtime Command Admin page None Admin → Operations → Download backup API (scriptable) None curl -X POST https://tessera.example.com/api/admin/backup -H "Authorization: Bearer <admin token>" -H "x-tessera-csrf: 1" -o backup.tar.gz Command line Stop first tessera backup --out backup.tar.gz [--include-key]

Restore with tessera restore backup.tar.gz --force while Tessera is stopped. Archives carry a SHA-256 manifest and restore refuses a tampered or truncated file.

docs.title: Production checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] HTTPS in front, TESSERA_SECURE_COOKIES=true, TESSERA_BASE_URL set
  • [ ] The data folder on a persistent, backed-up disk; master.key stored safely (or TESSERA_MASTER_KEY from a secret store)
  • [ ] Nightly backups, and one restore tried on a spare machine
  • [ ] SSO configured (Admin → Single sign-on) and the setup admin's password stored in a vault
  • [ ] TESSERA_TIMEZONE set for schedules; TESSERA_LOG_JSON=true if you ship logs
  • [ ] /metrics scraped with TESSERA_METRICS_TOKEN; /api/ready used as the health check
  • [ ] TESSERA_BLOCK_PRIVATE_HTTP=true if REST connectors must not reach your internal network
  • [ ] Email configured (Admin → Email) so alerts and subscriptions can be delivered

See CONFIGURATION.md for every setting.

docs.title: Identity
docs.text:
• Single sign-on: OpenID Connect with PKCE (Entra ID, Okta, Google Workspace, Keycloak, Auth0). Admin → Single sign-on.
  • SCIM 2.0 provisioning: Admin → Provisioning. Generate a token and give the identity provider the tenant URL https://<host>/scim/v2. Supported: Users and Groups (list with eq filters, create, read, replace, patch, delete). Deleting or deactivating a user ends their sessions and revokes their API tokens; nothing is hard-deleted.
  • Group mappings: map an IdP group to a Tessera role and, optionally, to a workspace role. A user gets the highest role among their groups. Admin is never a default role.

docs.title: Workspaces
docs.text: Workspaces group dashboards, reports, notebooks and semantic models. The General workspace is organization-wide. Private workspaces are invisible to non-members, including in search and to AI agents and MCP clients. Workspace roles: viewer (read), contributor (create and edit; also needs the global analyst role), admin (manage members). Data access rules (roles, row-level security) apply inside every workspace.

docs.title: Sharing and embedding
docs.text: Off by default. Admin → Operations turns it on and lists the sites allowed to frame dashboards (frame-ancestors). Analysts who can contribute to a dashboard create links that expire after 1 to 365 days, optionally locked to the slicer values they have selected. Viewers of a link see the dashboard read-only with the creator's access narrowed by those filters; nothing else in Tessera is reachable with the token. Revoke links from the dashboard's Share dialog; turning sharing off revokes all of them.

docs.title: Demo mode
docs.text: The demo workspace (sample retail data and a guided tour) can be loaded at setup or later by an admin from the top bar. "Switch to real data" removes exactly what the demo created plus anything built on demo data, after listing it, and leaves users, roles, SSO, tokens, workspaces and settings alone.

docs.title: Container image
docs.text: Release images are published for amd64 and arm64 at ghcr.io/vvipinthomas/tessera:<version>. docker compose up -d --build builds from the included Dockerfile (Python virtual environment, non-root user 10001, /data volume, health check on /api/ready). The base image is a build argument: docker build --build-arg BASE=<your approved Python 3.11+ Debian/Ubuntu image> . for registries that mirror or harden their own bases.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text:
Endpoint Purpose GET /api/health Liveness GET /api/ready Readiness: metadata store and warehouse reachable (503 otherwise) GET /metrics Prometheus: request counts and latency histograms by route, rate-limit hits, users, datasets, alerts by state, pipeline runs by status, warehouse size. Needs TESSERA_METRICS_TOKEN or an admin session

Every response carries X-Request-ID (an incoming one is kept). With TESSERA_LOG_JSON=1 logs are JSON lines, including one access record per API call with the request ID. TESSERA_RATE_LIMIT (default 1200 per minute) limits each API token, session or IP; excess calls get HTTP 429 with Retry-After.

docs.title: Audit
docs.text: Every sign-in, change, query, export, agent and MCP tool call is recorded. Admin → Operations exports CSV or JSON lines for a date range (for your SIEM) and sets retention (at least 30 days, or keep forever). Read notifications older than 90 days and expired sessions are purged daily.

docs.title: Backup and restore
docs.text:
• Online: Admin → Operations → Download backup (or POST /api/admin/backup). Consistent snapshot of the metadata database (SQLite online backup) and the warehouse (after a checkpoint), plus uploaded files, with SHA-256 checksums in manifest.json.
  • Offline: tessera backup --out tessera.tar.gz [--include-key] with the server stopped.
  • Restore: tessera restore tessera.tar.gz [--force] into an empty data folder. Checksums are verified and unsafe archive paths are refused.

Include master.key only if the archive is stored securely; otherwise keep the key separately. Without it, stored connection secrets cannot be decrypted.

docs.title: What is not included
docs.text: Tessera runs on one node. There is no high-availability metadata store, multi-node query engine or zero-downtime upgrade. It has not had an independent penetration test. Plan capacity and recovery accordingly.

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text:
Tessera is meant to sit alongside the tools a team already has. This page covers how data gets in (streaming and batch), how it gets out (BI tools, warehouses, lakes) and how Tessera reports to the rest of the data stack (lineage, dbt, orchestrators, AI clients). Admins see most of this on Admin → Integrations.

  • Business applications: Salesforce, Dynamics 365, Microsoft 365 and more
  • Copying a whole database
  • Mirroring PostgreSQL (change data capture)
  • Merge loads and schema changes
  • Power BI, Excel and Tableau
  • Streaming sources
  • Lakehouse tables: Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg
  • SFTP drops
  • Delivering data to other systems
  • Microsoft Fabric, Databricks and Snowflake
  • OpenLineage (Purview, DataHub, Marquez, OpenMetadata)
  • dbt
  • Orchestrators (Airflow, Dagster, Prefect, ADF, CI)
  • AI clients over MCP
  • REST API

docs.title: Business applications
docs.text:
Connections → Connect an application has ready-made connections. Sign-in, paging and incremental loading are already set up: you fill in your own details (a subdomain, a tenant, a key), tick the objects you want and press Load selected. Tessera then creates a pipeline that you can schedule.

Application Sign-in Objects Loads only what changed Salesforce OAuth 2 client credentials (External Client App or Connected App) Account, Contact, Opportunity, Lead, Case, User, Campaign, Task All, by SystemModstamp Microsoft Dynamics 365 / Dataverse OAuth 2 (Entra app registered as an application user) accounts, contacts, opportunities, leads, systemusers, plus any table you name Built-in tables, by modifiedon Microsoft 365 (Graph) OAuth 2 (Entra app, application permissions) users, groups, SharePoint list items Full copy HubSpot Private app token contacts, companies, deals, tickets, products, line items Full copy Stripe Restricted key customers, charges, invoices, subscriptions, payment intents, refunds, products, prices, payouts New records, by created GitHub Fine-grained token repositories; issues, pull requests, commits and releases per repository Issues and commits Jira Cloud Email and API token issues (your JQL), projects Issues, by updated Zendesk Support Agent email and API token tickets, users, organizations, groups Full copy ServiceNow User and password incident, change_request, problem, sys_user, cmdb_ci, plus any table you name All, by sys_updated_on Shopify Admin API token orders, products, customers All, by updated_at Airtable Personal access token the tables you name Full copy

How the changes-only loads work:

  • The first run copies everything.
  • Each later run asks the application only for records changed since the newest change already loaded. It looks back a little (five minutes, or a day where the application compares times in the user's time zone).
  • It then merges the result on the record's id, so a changed record replaces its old version and is never duplicated.

Objects that load changes only are marked changes only on the connection page.

For any other service, use REST / JSON API with page, offset, cursor, next-link or Link-header paging and bearer, header, query, basic or OAuth 2 (client credentials or refresh token) sign-in. Tokens are fetched, cached and renewed automatically, and a rejected token gets one fresh sign-in and a retry.

How it is tested: the test suite checks every object of every template against a simulated API that pages and signs in the way the vendor documents. It also checks the exact change filter each application receives (SOQL, OData, JQL, ServiceNow encoded queries, and query parameters). The real services are not called in tests.

docs.title: Copying a whole database
docs.text:
On any database, warehouse, lake or file connection, choose Copy many tables → Choose tables. Tick the tables (or Select all), pick a schedule, and press Copy selected. Tessera creates one pipeline with a load step per table and decides how each table is loaded:

The table has Load A primary key and a change column (updated_at, modified, last_modified, SystemModstamp and similar, of a date, time or number type) merge: only changed rows, updated in place A change column but no key incremental: new rows appended Neither replace: full copy each run

The result shows what was detected for each table, and you can edit any step afterwards. Over the API: POST /api/connections/{id}/copy with {"tables": [...], "prefix": "crm", "mode": "auto", "schedule": "0 * * * *"}.

docs.title: Mirroring PostgreSQL
docs.text:
Mirroring keeps tables continuously in step with a PostgreSQL database using its change log (logical decoding), without reloading. Inserts, updates, deletes and truncates arrive within seconds, and the tables are not queried again after the first copy.

On the database (once):

-- postgresql.conf: wal_level = logical   (then restart)
ALTER ROLE tessera_reader REPLICATION;   -- Amazon RDS / Aurora: GRANT rds_replication TO tessera_reader;
Service Setting to turn on Amazon RDS / Aurora PostgreSQL parameter group rds.logical_replication = 1 Azure Database for PostgreSQL server parameter wal_level = logical Google Cloud SQL flag cloudsql.logical_decoding = on Supabase, Neon, Crunchy Bridge logical replication is available; check the provider's setting

Every mirrored table needs a primary key. Nothing is installed on the database: Tessera uses the built-in test_decoding output plugin.

In Tessera: open the PostgreSQL connection, then Mirror tables → Choose tables → Start mirroring. Tessera:

  1. creates a replication slot (tessera_mirror_<id>), then takes a first copy of each table;
  2. every few seconds (TESSERA_MIRROR_SECONDS, default 5) reads the next batch of changes, applies them per table as one merge, and only then tells the database it may discard them. A crash in between replays the batch: changes are applied at least once and the merge makes that safe;
  3. fills in large unchanged values (which the change log leaves out) by reading the row from the source.

Connections lists every mirror with its status, changes applied, how far behind it is (in bytes of change log), and Sync now, Pause and Stop. Stopping a mirror drops its replication slot. A connection with mirrors cannot be deleted until they are stopped, because a forgotten slot makes the database keep change log indefinitely.

Limits: one database per mirror; column renames arrive as a new column; mirroring for SQL Server, MySQL and MongoDB is on the roadmap.

docs.title: Merge loads and schema changes
docs.text:
Merge is a fourth load mode next to replace, append and incremental. Give the key column(s) ({"key": ["id"]} in a pipeline step, or Key column(s) on the connection page). Rows whose key already exists are replaced, and new keys are added. If a key appears twice in one load, the last row wins. With a cursor column, a merge also loads only changed rows.

Schema changes are recorded on every load:

  • columns the source added;
  • columns it stopped sending, recorded once;
  • columns whose type changed.

A column whose values no longer fit its type is widened, never truncated: an integer column that starts receiving 25.5 becomes a decimal column. The owner and admins get a notification naming the downstream tables to check. The history is under Catalog → dataset → Schema history, and from GET /api/datasets/{id}/schema-changes.

docs.title: Power BI, Excel and Tableau
docs.text:
Tessera publishes a read-only OData v4 feed at https://<your tessera>/odata. It lists:

  • every published dataset (the serving zone), and
  • every saved report the token's owner can see, including reports built on semantic models, so Power BI shows the same certified Revenue as Tessera.

Masking and row-level security apply exactly as in the app: a token owned by a BC regional manager returns only BC rows. Raw and curated data are never exposed.

Create a token. Admin → API tokens (or API tokens for non-admins) → Create token, role viewer or analyst.

Power BI Desktop. Get data → OData feed → paste the URL → Basic: any user name, the token as the password → choose tables → Load. For scheduled refresh in the Power BI service, the URL must be reachable from Microsoft's cloud, or go through an on-premises data gateway.

Excel. Data → Get Data → From Other Sources → From OData Feed → URL → Basic, token as the password.

Tableau. Connect → To a Server → OData → URL → user name (anything) and the token as the password.

Query options supported: $select, $filter (eq, ne, gt, ge, lt, le, and, or, not, parentheses, contains, startswith, endswith, tolower, toupper, year, month, day, length, null), $orderby, $top, $skip, $count and server-driven paging (@odata.nextLink, 5,000 rows per page, or Prefer: odata.maxpagesize=n up to 50,000). Every row has a synthetic __row key. Each read is recorded in the audit log.

docs.title: Streaming sources
docs.text:
Data → Streams. A stream reads a source continuously and appends to a raw table. Events arrive in micro-batches (up to max events per batch, or whatever arrived within max wait, default 2 seconds).

Source Connection type Position saved Apache Kafka, Confluent Cloud, Redpanda, Amazon MSK, Aiven, WarpStream Kafka Offset per partition Azure Event Hubs (Standard tier and above, through its Kafka endpoint) Azure Event Hubs Offset per partition Amazon Kinesis Data Streams Kinesis Sequence number per shard MQTT (Mosquitto, EMQX, HiveMQ, AWS IoT Core, Azure Event Grid MQTT) MQTT Broker-side, QoS 1 persistent session Anything that can POST JSON: webhooks, Segment, Snowplow, your apps none (HTTP push) Each request is stored before the reply

Delivery guarantee. At least once. Tessera saves a stream's position only after the batch is in the warehouse, so a crash or restart re-reads the last batch rather than losing it. Set De-duplicate on column (for example event_id) to make replays harmless; the latest event per key is kept.

What lands. Your event fields as columns (nested objects are flattened, new fields add columns automatically), plus _key, _partition, _offset, _event_time (broker time) and _ingested_at. Payloads that are not valid JSON go to <table>__rejects with the raw text and the reason, and the stream keeps going.

Operations. Each stream shows status, events per minute, consumer lag (Kafka) or time behind latest (Kinesis), rows landed, rejects and the last error. Failing streams retry with back-off and are listed by the data health AI tool. Streams that were running start again when Tessera restarts. Retention trims rows older than N days, hourly. Preview reads a few events from the saved position without moving it. Reset position jumps to earliest or latest.

HTTP push. Creating an HTTP push stream shows a token once:

curl -X POST https://tessera.example.com/api/streams/7/events \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer tsk_..." -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '[{"event_id":"e-1","type":"signup","plan":"pro"}]'

It accepts one object, an array, {"events": [...]} or NDJSON (Content-Type: application/x-ndjson), up to 5 MB or 50,000 events per request. A 200 response means the events are stored.

Live dashboards. Build tiles on the stream's table (after a transform and publish, or directly in SQL for engineers), then press Live on the dashboard to refresh every 5 seconds.

Event Hubs settings. Namespace (for example contoso-events) and a connection string with Listen rights. Each event hub is a topic. Confluent Cloud: security SASL_SSL, mechanism PLAIN, API key and secret. Amazon MSK with IAM auth is not supported yet; use SASL/SCRAM.

Limits. This is micro-batch ingestion into one server, not a stream processor. Avro and Protobuf payloads with a schema registry are on the roadmap; today payloads are JSON or text.

docs.title: Lakehouse tables: Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg
docs.text:
Delta Lake connections read tables from a folder Tessera may access, or from s3://, abfss:// (Azure Data Lake and OneLake) and gs:// paths with storage options. Pick a version to time-travel; use a cursor column for incremental loads.

Apache Iceberg connections use a catalog:

Catalog Settings REST (Apache Polaris, Snowflake Open Catalog, Unity Catalog's Iceberg REST, Nessie, Lakekeeper, Tabular) URI, warehouse, token or client_id:secret AWS Glue Catalog glue, region in extra properties ({"glue.region": "us-east-1"}) Hive metastore URI thrift://host:9083 SQL (shared with PyIceberg or Spark's JDBC catalog) Database URI, warehouse, catalog name

Load by namespace.table, optionally with a row filter pushed down to the scan (amount > 0 and region = 'west'), a snapshot id for time travel, and a cursor column for incremental loads. Storage credentials for S3, ADLS or GCS go in extra properties using PyIceberg's names (for example s3.access-key-id).

docs.title: SFTP drops
docs.text:
The SFTP connection signs in with a password or a private key and reads CSV, JSON, Parquet or Excel files that match a pattern such as daily/*.csv.

  • Pin the host key. Leave Host key fingerprint empty, press Test, check the SHA256:... value with the server's owner, and paste it in. From then on Tessera refuses to connect if the server's key changes.
  • Only new files. Use mode incremental with cursor column _source_modified. Files that have not changed since the last load are not downloaded again. Each row records _source_file and _source_modified.

docs.title: Delivering data to other systems
docs.text:
Add a Deliver step to a pipeline to push a published dataset out after it is refreshed:

Destination connection Result PostgreSQL, SQL Server / Azure SQL / Fabric Warehouse, Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks SQL, Redshift, MySQL, Oracle, Trino, ClickHouse, SQLite, any SQLAlchemy database A table (name, schema.name or db.schema.name), replaced or appended Delta Lake (local, S3, ADLS/OneLake, GCS) A Delta table at a relative folder such as gold/orders S3 or Files A Parquet or CSV file

Only published data can leave, so masking has always been applied. The destination appears in lineage as dest:<connection>/<table>. Use a separate connection with write permission for deliveries; keep source connections read-only.

{"id": "to_snowflake", "type": "deliver", "depends_on": ["publish"], "dataset": "serving.orders",
 "connection_id": 4, "table": "ANALYTICS.PUBLIC.ORDERS", "mode": "replace"}

docs.title: Microsoft Fabric, Databricks and Snowflake
docs.text:
• Read from Fabric: the SQL Server connector reaches a Fabric Warehouse or Lakehouse SQL endpoint; the Delta connector reads OneLake tables at abfss://<workspace>@onelake.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com/<item>.Lakehouse/Tables.
  • Write to Fabric: deliver to a Delta folder in OneLake, or to a Fabric Warehouse through the SQL Server connector. Power BI in Fabric can also read Tessera directly through OData.
  • Databricks: read and deliver through Databricks SQL; read Unity Catalog tables as Delta, or through Unity Catalog's Iceberg REST endpoint with the Iceberg connector.
  • Snowflake: read and deliver through the Snowflake connector; read Iceberg tables in Snowflake Open Catalog through the Iceberg connector.

These driver connectors use each vendor's standard SQLAlchemy driver and are not exercised by Tessera's test suite; install the extra (tessera[snowflake], tessera[databricks], tessera[sqlserver]) on the server.

docs.title: OpenLineage
docs.text:
Admin → Integrations → OpenLineage. Turn it on, give the collector URL (Tessera posts to <URL>/api/v1/lineage unless the URL already ends in /lineage), a namespace and an optional API key (sent as a Bearer token, stored encrypted). Send test event checks the connection.

For every pipeline run Tessera sends START, then COMPLETE, FAIL (with the error) or ABORT. Completed events list the run's inputs (connections, uploads, streams, upstream tables) and outputs, with each output's column schema. Compatible collectors include Marquez, DataHub, OpenMetadata, Atlan, Astronomer and Microsoft Purview (through its OpenLineage support). If the collector is down, the run still succeeds and its log says the event was not delivered.

docs.title: dbt
docs.text:
Admin → Integrations → dbt → Import target/manifest.json from any dbt project (dbt Core or Cloud artifacts). Tessera matches dbt sources to raw datasets and models to published, then curated, then raw datasets by table name, and brings over:

  • model and column descriptions, owners (meta.owner) and tags (plus a dbt tag),
  • not_null, unique and accepted_values tests as quality rules with the same severity,
  • the model dependency graph as lineage.

Importing again updates descriptions and adds only new rules. Models with no matching dataset are listed so you can load them. Over the API: curl -F file=@target/manifest.json -H "Authorization: Bearer <engineer token>" https://<tessera>/api/integrations/dbt.

docs.title: Orchestrators
docs.text:
Create an API token with the engineer role and call:

curl -X POST https://tessera.example.com/api/pipelines/3/run -H "Authorization: Bearer tsr_..."
# {"run_id": 128}
curl https://tessera.example.com/api/runs/128 -H "Authorization: Bearer tsr_..."
# {"status": "running" | "success" | "failed", "steps": {...}, "log": [...]}

Airflow

from airflow.providers.http.operators.http import HttpOperator
from airflow.providers.http.sensors.http import HttpSensor

run = HttpOperator(task_id="tessera_orders", http_conn_id="tessera", endpoint="/api/pipelines/3/run", method="POST",
                   headers={"Authorization": "Bearer {{ var.value.tessera_token }}"}, response_filter=lambda r: r.json()["run_id"])
wait = HttpSensor(task_id="tessera_orders_done", http_conn_id="tessera",
                  endpoint="/api/runs/{{ ti.xcom_pull('tessera_orders') }}",
                  headers={"Authorization": "Bearer {{ var.value.tessera_token }}"},
                  response_check=lambda r: r.json()["status"] in ("success", "failed"), poke_interval=15)
run >> wait

Azure Data Factory / Fabric Data pipelines: a Web activity (POST to /api/pipelines/<id>/run) followed by an Until loop with a Web activity on /api/runs/<run_id>. Dagster, Prefect, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI: the same two HTTP calls. Pipelines can also POST a completion event to any webhook (Teams, Slack, PagerDuty).

docs.title: AI clients over MCP
docs.text: Claude Desktop, Claude Code, IDE assistants and your own agents connect to https://<your tessera>/mcp with an API token and get governed tools, datacards and prompts with the token owner's permissions. See MCP.md.

docs.title: REST API
docs.text: Everything the app does goes through a documented REST API. The interactive reference is at /api/docs on your server and the OpenAPI description at /api/openapi.json. Authenticate with Authorization: Bearer <token>.

docs.title: Tessera MCP server
docs.text: Tessera includes a Model Context Protocol server, so Claude Desktop, Claude Code, IDE assistants and your own agents can work with governed data without copying it anywhere.

docs.title: Connect
docs.text:
1. Create an API token under Admin → API tokens (or API tokens for non-admins). Pick the lowest role that does the job: a viewer token can search the catalog and glossary; an analyst token can also query semantic models and run read-only SQL on published data; an engineer token adds pipeline runs, run logs and raw/curated data.
  2. Connect a client.

Claude Code (Streamable HTTP)

claude mcp add --transport http tessera https://tessera.example.com/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer tsr_..."

Claude Desktop and other stdio clients (Tessera must be installed on that machine; it only relays messages):

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "tessera": {
      "command": "tessera",
      "args": ["mcp", "--url", "https://tessera.example.com"],
      "env": { "TESSERA_TOKEN": "tsr_..." }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: What it exposes
docs.text:
Kind Items Tools (read-only) search_catalog, glossary, list_datasets, describe_dataset, get_datacard, lineage_impact, data_health, profile_dataset, suggest_rules, readiness_report, run_sql, list_models, query_model, executive_brief, find_insights, explain_change, decompose, propose_chart, suggest_model, recent_runs, run_details, list_connections, draft_pipeline Tools (write, off by default) create_rule, run_quality, update_description Resources tessera://catalog, tessera://glossary, tessera://dataset/{schema}.{table} (datacard), tessera://model/{id} Prompts leadership-update, explain-metric-change, triage-data-incident, document-dataset

Tools are filtered by the token's role; tools the token cannot use are neither listed nor callable. Tool annotations mark read-only tools so clients can skip confirmation for them.

docs.title: Guarantees
docs.text:
• Same permissions as the web app. Calls run as the token's user with the token's role: row-level security, the serving-only rule for viewers and analysts, and workspace visibility all apply.
  • PII firewall. Values that look like emails, SINs, SSNs, card numbers, phones or IPs, and columns classified as personal data, are redacted before results leave Tessera, unless an admin has explicitly turned that off.
  • Writes are opt-in. An admin enables them under Admin → MCP server, and only engineer tokens get them.
  • Audited. Every call is recorded as mcp.tool with timing and arguments.
  • Protected. Bearer token required; browser Origin headers from other sites are rejected (DNS-rebinding protection); per-caller rate limits apply.

docs.title: Protocol notes
docs.text: Protocol versions 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05. Stateless JSON responses on POST /mcp (no server-sent event stream, no sessions); GET /mcp returns 405 as the specification allows. Batches are accepted for older clients.

docs.title: Tessera user guide
docs.text:
This guide walks through Tessera screen by screen. It is organised by what you want to get done, so you can jump to the part you need. If your Tessera has demo data loaded, every example below works on it as you read.

Contents

  1. Getting started
  2. Finding your way around
  3. For everyone: dashboards, questions and briefs
  4. For analysts: explore, reports, SQL, notebooks, alerts
  5. For engineers: connections, streams, pipelines, quality
  6. Semantic models, catalog and glossary
  7. AI agents and AI clients
  8. Using Tessera from Power BI, Excel and Tableau
  9. For admins
  10. Troubleshooting and FAQ

docs.title: First sign-in (the person who installs Tessera)
docs.text:
1. Open Tessera in a browser. On a fresh install you see Set up Tessera.
  2. Enter the setup code. It is printed in the server console and saved as setup-code.txt in the data folder (Docker: docker compose logs tessera | grep "Setup code").
  3. Enter your name, work email and a password of at least 12 characters. You become the first admin.
  4. Leave Start in demo mode ticked if you want to learn with sample data. Tessera loads a retail workspace (orders, customers, a certified Sales model, a dashboard, an alert, a notebook and a live checkout stream) and starts a guided tour.

docs.title: Demo mode and the tour
docs.text:
While demo data is loaded, the top bar shows Demo data, Take the tour and Switch to real data.

  • Take the tour walks through every main screen (about 25 short steps). Press Next or Back; close it with ✕ at any time.
  • Switch to real data shows exactly what will be removed, including anything you built on demo data, then deletes it. Users, roles, SSO, tokens and settings stay. An admin can load the demo again from the same place.

docs.title: Signing in later
docs.text: Use your email and password, or Sign in with single sign-on if your admin has set it up. Five wrong passwords lock the account for a while; an admin can unlock it.

docs.title: Roles in one line each
docs.text:
Role You can Viewer Open dashboards, reports and briefs, ask questions, read the catalog Analyst Also explore data, write SQL on published data, build reports and dashboards, set alerts, use AI agents Engineer Also connect sources, run streams and pipelines, write quality rules, publish data Admin Also manage users, SSO, email, AI providers, row-level security, integrations and backups

If a menu item or button is missing, your role does not include it.

docs.title: 2. Finding your way around
docs.text:
• The left rail groups screens: Analyze (Dashboards, Explore, Reports, Notebooks, SQL, AI agents), Data (Catalog, Semantic models, Glossary, Connections, Streams, Pipelines, Transforms) and Operate (Monitor, Alerts, Workspaces, Admin). The current screen is marked with a small green tile.
  • Search (top bar, or Ctrl K / ⌘ K) finds datasets, measures, dashboards, reports and glossary terms. Type a question and pick Ask: to get a chart straight away.
  • The bell shows notifications: alerts that fired, failed pipeline runs, shared items.
  • Home shows data health at a glance: dataset count, quality rules, published datasets, AI readiness per dataset and pipeline runs over the last two weeks.
  • Tessera follows your system's light or dark setting and works on phones (the rail becomes a top bar).

docs.title: 3. For everyone: dashboards, questions and briefs
Reading a dashboard
docs.text:
Open Dashboards and pick one.

  • Filters across the top (date range with presets, drop-downs with multi-select) apply to every tile.
  • Click a bar or slice to filter the whole page by it (cross-filtering). The active cross-filter appears as a chip; click its ✕ to clear it, or use Reset filters.
  • Change the time grain of a line chart (day, week, month, quarter, year) with the selector on the tile.
  • Tile menu (⋯): View data, Explain change and Deep dive (on tiles built from a semantic model).
  • Views ▾ saves the current filters as a named view and switches between saved views.
  • Refresh reloads now. Live refreshes every 5 seconds while the tab is visible, for dashboards on streaming data; it remembers your choice for that dashboard in this browser.
  • Excel exports every tile with the current filters. Print / PDF prints a clean page. TV mode goes full screen and refreshes every minute.

docs.title: Insights and Ask AI
docs.text:
• ✦ Insights opens a side panel of automated facts about the measures on the page: the latest change and what drove it, the trend, unusual points, a forecast and how concentrated the result is. Each fact says how it was worked out. Summarise with AI writes a short summary using only those facts (needs an AI provider).
  • Ask AI answers questions about the dashboard in a chat, using the same governed measures. Every number in an answer is checked against the data; a badge shows whether all figures were verified.
  • Explain change (tile menu) splits a change between two periods across every dimension and ranks what moved it most. Deep dive opens a decomposition tree: start from the total and split by any dimension, or let Tessera pick the split that stands out.

docs.title: The executive brief
docs.text:
Press Executive brief on any dashboard. For each measure you see:

  • the latest period against the previous one and the same period last year, year to date, and momentum (whether year-over-year growth is speeding up or slowing down),
  • the full-year forecast with its likely range, and the chance of hitting the target (admins and analysts set targets with Targets),
  • a what-if slider: drag it to see where the year lands if the rest of the year runs higher or lower,
  • the drivers behind the change and the segments trending up or down.

The headline list at the top ranks what leadership should know first. Monthly / Quarterly switches the view. Copy summary copies the headlines as text; Email weekly subscribes people to the brief by email; Print / PDF makes a handout. Forecasts state their method (for example seasonal Holt-Winters) and how accurate it was on recent history.

docs.title: Asking questions in plain English
docs.text:
In Explore (or the search bar), type a question such as:

  • top 5 provinces by revenue last quarter
  • monthly orders in BC since 2026-03
  • refund rate by channel excluding store this year

Tessera shows Understood as: with the measure, breakdown, filters and time range it used, and lists any words it did not understand. It uses certified definitions and glossary synonyms (so sales finds Revenue if the glossary says so). No AI provider is needed.

docs.title: Shared links
docs.text: If someone sends you a Tessera share link, it opens a read-only copy of a dashboard without signing in. Links expire, can be revoked, and may be locked to filters (for example only BC).

docs.title: 4. For analysts: explore, reports, SQL, notebooks, alerts
Explore and reports
docs.text:
1. Explore → pick a model (for example Sales).
  2. Tick measures (Revenue, Orders) and dimensions (Province, Order date). Choose a time grain next to date dimensions.
  3. Add filters with + Add filter.
  4. Pick a visual: Auto, KPI, Bar, Line, Area, Lines, Combo, Donut, Treemap, Stacked, Waterfall, Funnel, Scatter, Pivot or Table. Options include Compare with previous period, Forecast, Flag anomalies and a Target line.
  5. Save as report, Add to dashboard, Create alert, or export to Excel / CSV. Generated SQL shows the exact query.

Reports lists saved reports; open one to change it, export it or add it to a dashboard.

docs.title: Building a dashboard
docs.text:
1. Dashboards → New dashboard, then Edit.
  2. Add tile (a saved report or a text tile) and Add filter (a date range or a drop-down on a model field).
  3. Drag tiles to reorder; drag a tile's right edge to resize it on a 12-column grid; choose short, medium or tall in each tile's height selector.
  4. Press Done. Share creates a read-only link or embed code if your admin has turned sharing on.
  5. Subscribe emails the dashboard on a schedule, with an Excel or CSV attachment and optionally the executive brief at the top.

docs.title: SQL
docs.text: SQL runs read-only queries on published data (serving.*; engineers can also read raw and curated). The left panel lists tables and columns; click a column to insert it. Run (Ctrl+Enter), then pick a chart type to visualise the result and Save as chart to reuse it. Only one SELECT runs at a time, and queries stop after 60 seconds.

docs.title: Notebooks
docs.text: Notebooks → New notebook mixes Markdown and SQL cells, each SQL cell with its own chart. Run all refreshes every cell. Notebooks are visible to everyone who can see their workspace.

docs.title: Alerts and subscriptions
docs.text: Alerts → New alert watches a model measure, a report value, a dataset's quality, data freshness or pipeline failures, on a schedule. Choose the condition (for example Refund rate above 8%) and where to send it: in the app, by email or to a webhook (Teams, Slack). Check now tests it immediately. Alerts and subscriptions run with your permissions, including row-level security.

docs.title: 5. For engineers: connections, streams, pipelines, quality
Connecting a source
docs.text:
1. Connections → New connection, choose the connector, name it, fill in the fields. Use a read-only account. Passwords and keys are encrypted and never shown again.
  2. Save and test. Browse lists tables, files, topics or collections.
  3. On the connection page, Load data: choose the table or path, the target table (for example raw.orders) and a mode:
  4. replace: reload everything,
  5. append: add rows,
  6. incremental: add only rows whose cursor column (for example updated_at) is newer than last time.
  7. merge: give the key column(s) (for example id); rows with a key that already exists are updated, new ones added. Add a cursor column to load only changed rows. For SFTP, use the cursor column _source_modified to load only new or changed files. For Iceberg, add a row filter or a snapshot id; for Delta, a version.
  8. Upload file on the Catalog page loads a CSV, Excel, JSON or Parquet file directly.

docs.title: Connecting a business application
docs.text: Connections → Connect an application, then pick the application (Salesforce, Dynamics 365, Microsoft 365, HubSpot, Stripe, GitHub, Jira, Zendesk, ServiceNow, Shopify or Airtable). The form asks only for what is yours, such as your subdomain, tenant or key, and links to the vendor's instructions for creating it. Save and test, tick the objects and press Load selected. Objects marked changes only load just what changed on later runs. Open the pipeline it creates to put it on a schedule. Details for each application: INTEGRATIONS.md.

docs.title: Copying many tables at once
docs.text: On a database, warehouse, lake or file connection, Copy many tables → Choose tables, tick them (or Select all), choose Smart and a schedule, and press Copy selected. Smart merges tables that have a primary key and a change column such as updated_at. It appends new rows for tables with only a change column, and fully copies the rest. The result lists what it detected for each table.

docs.title: Mirroring a PostgreSQL database
docs.text: For tables that must stay current within seconds, open a PostgreSQL connection, Mirror tables → Choose tables → Start mirroring. Tessera takes a first copy, then follows every insert, update and delete from the database's change log. The database needs wal_level = logical, the user needs the REPLICATION attribute, and each table needs a primary key; see INTEGRATIONS.md. Mirrors are listed on Connections with Sync now, Pause and Stop. Stop a mirror when you no longer need it, so the database stops keeping change log for it.

docs.title: When a source changes its columns
docs.text:
Every load compares the columns with the previous one. New columns are added and widened types are kept, so a decimal arriving in a whole-number column is never rounded. Removed columns are kept with empty values. The owner and admins get a notification that names the downstream tables to check. Catalog → dataset → Schema history shows every change.

The connector catalog at the bottom of Connections shows which connectors are verified by Tessera's tests and which need a driver installed on the server.

docs.title: Streams
docs.text:
Streams shows each stream's status, events per minute, rows landed and lag. To add one:

  1. Create a Kafka, Azure Event Hubs, Kinesis or MQTT connection first (HTTP push needs none).
  2. Streams → New stream, choose the source kind, the connection, the topic or stream name, and the table to land in (for example raw.orders_live).
  3. Choose the payload (JSON, or text stored in a value column) and where to start (From the beginning or Only new events).
  4. Optional, under Batching, de-duplication and retention: batch size and wait, a de-duplicate on column such as event_id, and how many days to keep.
  5. Create and start. For HTTP push, copy the endpoint and token from the dialog; it is shown once.

On a stream's page: Stop / Start, Preview (reads a few events without moving the position; stop the stream first), Reset position (earliest or latest), Rotate token (HTTP push), Query latest rows. Events that are not valid JSON go to <table>__rejects with the reason. If the source is unreachable the status becomes retrying with the error shown, and the stream recovers on its own.

docs.title: Pipelines
docs.text:
Pipelines → New pipeline builds a graph of steps. Each step has an id, the steps it runs after, and retries.

Step Does Ingest Loads from a connection into raw (or curated) Transform Runs a SELECT into a curated table Quality Runs the dataset's rules; fails the run on error rules, any failing rule, or never Scan for personal data Detects personal data and proposes masking Publish Writes the masked copy to serving Deliver Writes a published dataset to a database, warehouse, Delta lake, S3 or folder Export Writes Parquet or CSV with a datacard Webhook Calls a URL Trigger another pipeline Chains pipelines
